Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verse 1:

(p-5126) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah az-Zumar

It was named after the verse in which the "groups" (zumar) of the two parties are mentioned, which points to the detailed recompense, the establishment of proof, and the nullification of excuses. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. So said al-Mahayimi. It is a Meccan surah, though some excepted three verses: ﴿Say: O My servants﴾ [az-Zumar: 53] and so on... on the view that they were revealed concerning Wahshi, the slayer of Hamzah, according to what has been narrated. It is said that a fourth is ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾ [az-Zumar: 23], related by Ibn al-Jawzi, and discussion of the like of this has already preceded.

Its verses number seventy-five.

al-Nasa'i related from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fast until we said he would not break it, and he would break it until we said he would not fast.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite, every night, Bani Isra'il and az-Zumar.

(p-5127) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1] ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾

﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾: i.e., this is a revelation, or its revelation is from Allah.

It is also read (tanzila) in the accusative, by supposing a verb (implied).

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾.

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾ means: free from the branches of polytheism and ostentation, by purifying monotheism (tawhid) and cleansing the inner heart (sirr).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verse 3:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Surely, to God belongs pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him say, "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position." Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾

﴿Surely, to God belongs pure religion﴾ That is, the religion whose exclusivity is due to Him, such that obedience is to be made sincerely for Him, free from every impurity, because He alone is the one deserving of divinity. ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him﴾ That is, in love, seeking nearness to God and intercession through them: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position.﴾ That is, they say this as an argument in defense of their misguidance. ﴿Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ.﴾ That is, at the gathering of their objects of worship with them, He will pair each of them with those who take them as allies, the worshipper with the worshipped, and He will cause the falsifier to enter the Fire along with the falsifiers, just as He causes the one of truth to enter Paradise along with the people of truth. ﴿Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever﴾ meaning, He does not lead him to salvation and the abode of the righteous.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[4] ﴿If Allah had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from among what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾

﴿If Allah had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from among what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ That is: declare Him far above likeness, similarity, and the choosing of a son, because oneness is inherent in His essence, and His subjugation of others is by His oneness. There is no likeness in existence, so how could there be likeness in necessary existence?

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verses 5–6:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[5–6] ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock in pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ — that is, by removing one of them and covering the other in its place, as if the one were clothed in it and wrapped around it. ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾ — which is the end of its cycle, or the cessation of its motion. ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — that is, from its own self and kind: (p-5129) ﴿its mate﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. ﴿And He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — that is, male and female, from the camels, the cattle, the sheep and the goats. ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — that is, passing through stages of formation. ﴿In three darknesses﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — meaning the belly, the womb, and the amniotic membrane. ﴿That is﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — that is, the Creator of your forms. The Wrapper, that is, the One who directs by His power, who subjects by His dominion, who brings the multitude into being from a single soul by His wisdom, and who sends down blessings by His favour. ﴿Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6] — that is, away from His worship toward the worship of others.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verse 7:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts.﴾

﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you﴾, i.e., free of need of your faith. ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾, i.e., because it is the cause of their destruction. ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾, i.e., if you employ what He has bestowed upon you in that for which it was created, He accepts it from you, because it is His religion, and He rewards you with a good reward for your obedience.

Note:

In "al-Iklil", it is cited as evidence, from His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾, that He, exalted is He, does not approve of disbelief and sins, and that approval (al-ridha') is other than will (al-irada). This is one of the two positions of the people of the Sunnah. The second position, which al-Amidi related from the majority, is that approval and will are equivalent, and they interpreted "servants" (al-'ibad) in the verse as referring to the sincere ones. ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾, i.e., no bearing woman will carry the load of another, meaning what is upon her of sins, or: no soul will be seized for the sin of another soul, but rather each is seized for its own sin. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾, i.e., after death. ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾, i.e., of what is in the hearts of good and evil.

(p-5130)

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[8–9] ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He grants him a blessing from Himself, he forgets what he was calling upon Him for before, and sets up rivals to God, to lead others astray from His way. Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."﴾ ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [equal to the disbeliever]? Say: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only those of understanding remember.﴾ [al-Zumar: 8–9]

﴿And when it touches﴾, i.e., befalls, ﴿man, harm﴾, i.e., hardship and affliction, ﴿he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾, i.e., he earnestly entreats Him to remove the hardship and affliction from him, turning to Him in supplication and humble entreaty. ﴿Then when He grants him﴾, i.e., gives him, ﴿a blessing from Himself, he forgets what he was calling upon Him for before﴾, i.e., he forgets the harm which he had been calling upon God to remove before the blessing. It has also been said: he forgets his Lord, whom he had been humbly beseeching and earnestly entreating. The word ﴿ma﴾ (what) here carries the meaning of ﴿man﴾ (who); it is used in its place for the purpose of descriptive supplication, and because of the vagueness and grandeur conveyed by ﴿ma﴾. ﴿And sets up rivals to God, to lead others astray from His way﴾, i.e., to turn people away from His religion and obedience. ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief"﴾, i.e., live by it, ﴿for a little while﴾, i.e., briefly, in this world.

﴿Indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire﴾. ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., one who is devoted in worship during its hours, spending them in prostration and standing. ﴿Fearing the Hereafter﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., its punishment. ﴿And hoping for the mercy of his Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., His Paradise and His good pleasure. That is, is this one better, or that disbelieving, denying one who forgets his Lord?

﴿Say: "Are those who know﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., His Oneness, His command, and His prohibition, equal in reward and obedience to ﴿those who do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]?" i.e., the two are not equal.

(p-5131)

Remarks:

First: The verse indicates the recommendation of night prayer. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "ānāʾ al-layl" means the middle of the night. Al-Hasan said: its hours, its beginning, its middle, and its end.

Second: His words, exalted is He, ﴿fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], are a refutation of those who condemn worship done out of fear of the Fire or hope for Paradise. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Around it we hum" (ﷺ).

Third: In His words, exalted is He, ﴿Are those [who know] equal﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], and the verse, there is praise of knowledge, the elevation of its status, and the condemnation of ignorance and its deficiency. It may be inferred from it that the ignorant person is not equal to the knowledgeable woman, just as he is not equal to the daughter of a scholar. This is what al-Iklil conveys.

The verse also implies that those who know are those who act upon their knowledge, since He first described them with the word ﴿qānit﴾ (devoutly obedient), and then negated equality between him and others, to emphasize this and to state explicitly that one who does not act upon knowledge is as if he were not knowledgeable.

Al-Qashani said: The obedient one is only the knowledgeable one because knowledge is that which has taken root in the heart and become firmly rooted in the soul, to the extent that its possessor cannot oppose it, but rather it is mingled with flesh and blood, so its effect appears in the limbs, and none of them is separated from its requirement. As for what is merely imprinted in the realm of imagination, such that the soul can be distracted from it and from its requirement, that is not knowledge. It is only a conceptual matter and a passing imagination that does not endure, but rather vanishes quickly; it does not nourish the heart, nor make it grow fat, nor satisfy hunger.

﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., they are admonished by this reminder, ﴿those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], i.e., the intellects pure of the husk of imagination and illusion, because they are realized in firmly rooted knowledge which affects the outward self. As for those mixed with illusion, they do not remember, nor are they realized in this knowledge, nor do they retain it.

(p-5130)

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[10] ﴿Say: O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and God's earth is spacious. Only the patient will be given their reward without measure.﴾

﴿Say: O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good﴾: that is, for those who do good through acts of obedience in this world, there is a good reward in the Hereafter, whose reality cannot be fully comprehended. ﴿And God's earth is spacious﴾: that is, His lands are many. Whoever finds it difficult to devote himself to doing good in his homeland should emigrate to where he can do so.

Al-Shihab said: The manner in which this construction conveys these many meanings has been clarified by the commentators of the Kashshaf, who explained that His saying ﴿for those who do good﴾ is a resumptive clause giving the reason for the command to be mindful of God, and for this reason it is qualified by the adverbial phrase "in this world," because this world is the farm of the Hereafter, so the seed of rewards should be sown in its tilth. He followed this sentence so that one could not excuse negligence on the grounds of the place not assisting, or justify it by refusing to leave one's homeland. It was therefore an urging to seize the opportunity of one's lifetime, to abandon what hinders one through love of one's dwellings, and to emigrate across whatever expanse of lands is available, as it has been said:

"If my origin is from dust, then all lands are my homeland, and all the people of the world are my kin."

End of quotation.

﴿Only the patient will be given their reward﴾: that is, those who endure the hardships of obedience, including bearing afflictions and leaving their homelands for its sake. ﴿Their reward without measure﴾: that is, without a measuring vessel; this is a figure of speech for abundance.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."﴾

﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."﴾ That is: free from turning toward anything other than Him.

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.﴾

﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.﴾ That is: I have been commanded with this, so that I may be their foremost (p-5133) in this world and the Hereafter; for his sincerity (ﷺ) is more complete than the sincerity of every sincere person. Based on this, "firstness" is in nobility and rank. Or, it means that he is the first of his community to submit his face to God. So "firstness" is temporal in its apparent sense. It is also permissible for the lam to be considered superfluous (zā'idah), as in: "I wanted to do" (aradtu li-an af'al). Then it becomes a command to take the lead in sincerity.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[13–14] "Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day." "Say: It is Allah I worship, sincerely devoting my religion to Him" [Az-Zumar: 14].

"Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord" — that is, by abandoning sincerity toward Him — "the punishment of a tremendous Day." "Say: It is Allah I worship" — that is, I single Him out for worship — "sincerely devoting my religion to Him" [Az-Zumar: 14] — free from the admixture of anything else.

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil, the deeper explanation of meaning) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[15] ﴿So worship what you will besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."﴾

﴿So worship what you will besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ That is: they destroyed themselves through misguidance, and their families through leading them astray. They lost themselves through perdition, and their families likewise, if the families were like them. Or they lost them through a separation with no reunion after it, if the families were among the people of Paradise. ﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.﴾

[16] "For them there will be layers of fire above them, and beneath them layers [of fire]. That is what Allah threatens His servants with. O My servants, so fear Me."

Layers of fire above them and beneath them: that is, tiers of fire. That is: the punishment promised with it. "With that Allah frightens His servants: O My servants, so fear Me": that is, by avoiding what brings about wrath. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is an admonition from Allah the Exalted and a far-reaching counsel.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verses 17–19:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17–19] ﴿And those who avoid the taghut (false deities), not worshipping them, and turn back in repentance to Allah – for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants,﴿who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 18] ﴿Then is he against whom the word of punishment has come [to be fulfilled] – can you save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 19].

﴿And those who avoid the taghut (ṭāghūt), not worshipping them﴾ means the idols. The form fa'alūt (ṭāghūt) is used for intensification (al-mubālaghah) [of the sense of transgression]. ﴿And turn back in repentance to Allah – for them is good news﴾, i.e., of reward. ﴿So give good tidings to My servants﴾ ﴿who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 18], i.e., preferring the most excellent and being concerned with the most perfect.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He meant that they should be critics in religion, distinguishing between the good (ḥasan) and the better (aḥsan), and between the virtuous (fāḍil) and the most virtuous (afḍal). This encompasses the schools of thought and the choice of the most firmly established of them in terms of their foundations (al-sabk), the strongest of them when examined (al-sabr), and the clearest of them in evidence and sign; and that you should not be in your school as the poet said:

"And do not be like a donkey that, when led, is led along."

He means the blind follower (al-muqallid). End of quote.

It also encompasses preferring the more excellent of any two kinds, [in cases of] conflict (i'tirāḍ), such as the obligatory over the recommended, pardon over retaliation, and concealment over disclosure in charity, and so on. ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [Az-Zumar: 18]. ﴿Then is he against whom the word of punishment has come [to be fulfilled] – can you save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 19], i.e., can you rescue him from it? That is, it is impossible at all to save him.

## Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verse 22:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon light from his Lord? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.﴾.

﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam﴾ meaning: He widened it for submitting one's face to Him alone, and for accepting His religion and His law, by His kindness, His care, and His support, glorified is He. ﴿So he is upon light from his Lord﴾ meaning: upon clear proof, knowledge, (p-٥١٣٦) and guidance to the truth. The metaphorical use of light for guidance and recognition (istiʿarah, metaphor) is well known, just as darkness is used metaphorically for its opposite. The predicate of (man, "one who") is omitted, indicated by His saying: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: from accepting His remembrance, due to the intensity of their inclination toward bodily pleasures and their turning away from holy perfections. Or it means: because of His remembrance. In that case (min, "from") is causal (taʿlil, expressing cause), and it also carries the sense of origination, since the hardness arises from it. Al-Shihab said: If it is said "qasa minhu" (it hardened from it), the meaning is that it is a cause of a hardness that arose from it. If it is said "qasa ʿanhu" (it hardened away from it), the meaning is that its hardness made him distant from accepting it, and both usages are attested. It has also been read with ʿan (ʿan, "from/away from") in the shadhdh (irregular, non-canonical) readings. However, the first is more eloquent, because hardness of the heart requires not remembering Allah, and that is its meaning when it is construed with ʿan. Remembrance of Him, exalted is He, is among the things that soften hearts. So His making it a cause of hardness indicates the intensity of disbelief, which He made the cause of softness into a cause of its hardening. ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾ meaning: away from the path of truth.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Allah has sent down the best of discourse, a Book consistent within itself, [oft-]repeated; the skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾

﴿Allah has sent down the best of discourse, a Book consistent within itself﴾, meaning: some of it resembles other parts of it, in soundness, firmness, being built upon truth, sincerity, benefit to mankind, and the aspects of its inimitability. ﴿[Oft-]repeated﴾ is the plural of (muthanna) (doubled, repeated), meaning reiterated and repeated, because its stories, reports, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats and admonitions are repeated. ﴿The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord﴾ is either a figurative expression for the extreme intensity of their fear, or a literal description of their being affected when they hear its verses, its wisdom and its threats, by what enters their hearts from them. ﴿Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: through submission, obedience and tranquility to His command. ﴿That﴾, meaning: the Book, or what arises from fear and hope. ﴿That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whomever Allah leaves astray﴾, meaning: whose heart deviates. ﴿For him there is no guide.﴾

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Is one who shields his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]? It will be said to the wrongdoers: "Taste what you used to earn."﴾

﴿Is one who shields his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection⦆ — i.e., whoever makes his face a shield against the severity of the punishment on that Day, standing in place of what would otherwise shield him, in that it is the first thing the painful torment touches. This is because what one normally protects himself with is his hands, and they are shackled. Had they not been shackled, he would have warded off [the punishment] from his face with them, since the face is the most honored of his limbs. It has also been said: shielding oneself with the face is a metaphor for the absence of anything with which one could shield oneself, since the face is not something one can shield with. The predicate of (man, "whoever") is omitted, as is the case with its counterparts; i.e., [it is like] the one who is secure from punishment. ﴿And it will be said to the wrongdoers: "Taste what you used to earn"﴾ — i.e., its consequence.

﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.﴾ That is: they do not expect that evil would come to them from it.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿An Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness, that they may be conscious of God.﴾

﴿An Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness﴾ means: upright, free from contradiction and discord. ﴿That they may be conscious of God﴾ means: that they may guard against the punishment and the disgrace of the Day of Recompense, by refraining from ugly deeds, vile characters and corrupt beliefs. And for the sake of those parables, by which is illustrated what one should guard against, the greatest of dreaded things, which is polytheism (shirk), His Glorified words are:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Allah sets forth a parable: a man belonging to several partners who quarrel with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two alike in comparison? All praise is due to Allah. But most of them do not know.﴾

﴿Allah sets forth a parable﴾ means: for the polytheist and the monotheist, two men who are slaves. ﴿A man belonging to several partners who quarrel with one another﴾ means: they are ill-natured; they pull him in different directions and take turns with him in their various affairs. He is always bewildered and his heart is divided, not knowing which of them to please with his service or on which of them to rely for his needs. ﴿And a man belonging wholly to one man﴾ means: his ownership is purely for him. He turns only toward his one master and travels only to serve him. So his concern is one, and his heart is unified. ﴿Are the two alike in comparison?﴾ means: in condition and state, that is, in good circumstances and peace of mind? No indeed. Such is the state of one who affirms many gods: he is always bewildered and fearful, not knowing which of them to worship or on whose lordship to rely. And the state of one who worships only one God has one concern and one purpose, with a tranquil mind and a comfortable life. The point is that the Oneness (tawhid) of the object of worship entails the unity of direction and the warding off of division. As Allah, exalted is He, related from Yusuf, peace be upon him: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39].

﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾. Abu al-Su'ud said: it is an affirmation of what precedes it, of the negation of equality, by way of parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD), and an alert to the monotheists that the distinction they possess is by Allah's grace, and that it is a great blessing which obliges them to persist in praising Him and worshipping Him. Or, it means that His clarifying through the striking of a parable is that for them is the highest parable, and for the polytheists is the parable of evil. It is a beautiful act and a complete kindness from Him, mighty and majestic, which deserves His praise and worship.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[30] ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.﴾

﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.﴾ This is a preface to what follows of disputing on the Day of Resurrection. It is also recited as "mā'it" and "mā'itūn." It was said: they were waiting for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to die. That is: all of you are on the verge of death.

[Verse 31] "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute."

"Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord": i.e., the Owner of your affairs. "Will dispute": i.e., you will argue against them, that you conveyed to them what you were sent with of rulings and admonitions, among which are those contained within these verses, and that you strove in calling to the truth with the utmost striving, while they persisted in obstinacy and stubborn opposition.

The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:

[32] ﴿Who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾

(p-5140) ﴿Who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah﴾: that is, who fabricates against Him by ascribing to Him a partner and a son. ﴿And denies the truth﴾: that is, the matter which is the very essence of the truth. ﴿When it comes to him﴾: that is, when its proof and its evidence have come before him, yet he rejects it and turns it back upon the one who brought it. Meaning: none of the disputants is more unjust than one whose condition is this, for he is more unjust than every wrongdoer. ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾: that is, for those who have fabricated against Allah, glorified is He, and hastened to deny the truth.

[38] ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended some harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended some mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely those who rely."﴾

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ This is because the acknowledgment of that is established in their natural dispositions (fitar) and intellects, and because the proof for it is clear. ﴿Say﴾, that is, as a rebuke to them: ﴿"Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended some harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended some mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?"﴾, that is, His benefit and goodness. The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 39, verses 39–40:

(p-542) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[39–40] ﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. So you will soon know, [40] who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 40].

﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your position"﴾ meaning: your state in which you are, of enmity and opposition to the truth. ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ meaning: according to my position. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 39, verse 41:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[41] ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, only to its detriment does he go astray. And you are not over them a manager.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth﴾ i.e., for their sake, and for their need of it and their dependence upon its clarification of their paths of guidance. ﴿So whoever is guided﴾ i.e., by its proofs, ﴿it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, only to its detriment does he go astray. And you are not over them a manager﴾ i.e., because of their obstinacy against guidance, since your duty is only to convey (the message). ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists﴾ [al-Hijr: 94].

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Statement, Exalted is He:

[42] ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He retains those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ meaning: their separation (from the bodies), by completely nullifying their control over them. ﴿And those that do not die during their sleep﴾ (p-5143) meaning: and He takes those whose death has not yet come during their sleep, by nullifying their activity through the outward senses. ﴿Then He retains those for which He has decreed death﴾ meaning: He does not return them to their bodies until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And releases the others until a specified term﴾ meaning: and that is another sleep, or death. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ meaning: in what has been mentioned of the taking (of souls) in both ways. ﴿Are signs for a people who reflect﴾ meaning: concerning the manner of their connection to the bodies and their taking away from them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession entirely. His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] ﴿When Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shudder; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45]

﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession entirely."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] That is: He is its owner. No one can intercede at all, unless the one being interceded for is approved and the intercessor is permitted to intercede, and both of these are absent here. ﴿His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] ﴿When Allah alone is mentioned﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45], that is, without their gods, ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shudder; but when those other than Him are mentioned﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45], that is, individually, or together with the mention of Allah Most High, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45], that is, they are delighted by that, due to the excess of their infatuation with them and their forgetfulness of the right of Allah Most High. Both matters have been emphasized, since He has clarified the extreme degree of each of them. Rejoicing (istibshar) is when the heart is filled with joy until the surface of the face is expanded by it, and shuddering (ishmi'zaz) is when the heart is filled with distress until the skin of the face is drawn tight.

(p-5144) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[46] ﴿Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they have been differing."﴾

﴿Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they have been differing."﴾ That is: take refuge in Allah through supplication, by His most beautiful names, and say: "You alone are able to judge between me and them." The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 39, verses 49–50:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[49–50] ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Those before them had already said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50]

(p-1145) ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of knowledge"﴾, meaning: from Me, by the ways of earning and acquiring. ﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾, meaning: a test for him, whether he will be grateful for that favor and direct it toward what it was created for, and thus be happy, or deny it and thus be wretched. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Those before them had already said it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50], meaning: as Qarun said, ﴿He said, "I have only been given it because of knowledge that is with me"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 78]. ﴿But what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50], meaning: what they gained through that knowledge of worldly goods did not avert from them.

[51–52] ﴿So the evil consequences of what they earned befell them. And as for those who wronged among these, the evil consequences of what they earned will befall them, and they will not escape.﴾ ﴿Have they not known that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts [it]? That is: [the proof is] that all of it is from Him, glory be to Him. Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ (p-514) ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, [after which you will not be helped]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54] ﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55] ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, how I regret my neglect concerning Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56].

﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾, i.e., who have wronged themselves by excess in sins and disbelief: ﴿do not despair﴾ — it is read with a fatha and with a kasra on the nun — ﴿of the mercy of Allah﴾, i.e., do not despair of His forgiveness by doing a means that erases the effect of excess: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾, i.e., for whoever repents and believes, for Islam wipes away what came before it: ﴿Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54], i.e., repent to Him: ﴿and submit to Him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54], i.e., surrender and yield to Him, which is by worshipping Him alone and obeying Him alone, by doing what He commanded and avoiding what He forbade: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, [after which you will not be helped]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54]. ﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55]. ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, how I regret﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56], i.e., how I fell short: ﴿my neglect concerning Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56], i.e., in regard to His command and prohibition, since I did not follow the best of what was sent down: ﴿and indeed I was among the mockers﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56], i.e., those who ridiculed those who follow the best.

And "أنْ تَقُولَ" (an taqula, "lest a soul should say") is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu) with an elided noun governing it, i.e., "so hasten to avoid the dislike that a soul should say"; or it is a causative explanation of a verb implied by what precedes it, i.e., "I warn you and command you to follow the best of speech, out of dislike [that a soul should say]." Its detailed treatment is in the "Shuruh al-Kashshaf" (commentaries on al-Kashshaf).

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[67] ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure, while the earth entire will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure, while the earth entire will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ That is: they did not assess His majesty, may He be exalted, with its true greatness, nor did they recognize His glory with its true recognition. They set up partners for Him and attributed to Him what does not befit His sublime affairs. Yet His greatness and the perfection of His power are such that the imagination is bewildered by them. For the replacing of the earth with another earth, and the folding of the heavens like the folding of a scroll, are the easiest of things for Him.

Regarding "the handful" (al-qabdah) and "the right hand" (al-yamin), there are two well-known positions:

The position of the early generations (al-salaf), which is to affirm these attributes without modality (takyif), without likening (tashbih), without distortion (tahrif), without alteration (tabdil), without change (taghyir), and without removing the noble wording from what the Arabs understand by it and apply it to, by way of interpretation. They take the apparent meaning and entrust its knowledge to God, may He be exalted. They acknowledge that its interpretation, that is, what it ultimately amounts to in reality, is known only to God. This is also their stance on all the attributes that the Qur'an has mentioned and that have come in authentic reports.

The second position: that this is a metaphor (majaz), well known in the speech of the Arabs, and that usage is not confined to the literal meaning. Among its proponents, some hold that the metaphor is in the individual words: "handful" (al-qabdah) is borrowed to mean dominion or disposal, and "right hand" (al-yamin) to mean power. Others hold that the metaphor is in the composition as a whole, by representing the state of His greatness and the penetrating reach of His power by the state of one who has a handful in which the earth lies and a right hand by which the heavens are folded. This is the view that al-Zamakhshari relied upon and expounded in the finest manner.

Then he pointed out that among the greatness of His power, may He be exalted, is that He made the blowing of the Trumpet (al-Sur) the cause of the death of all at one time and of their life at another, by His saying:

The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:

[68] ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.﴾

﴿And the Horn will be blown, and [whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth] will swoon﴾, i.e., will perish. ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾, i.e., from among the special angels, or from among the martyrs; this was related from some of the Successors (tabi'un). Qatadah said: "Allah has made an exception, and Allah knows best, to what it has become an exception." This is the correct view, since recourse is not had to clarifying what is ambiguous (mubhamat) except with a decisive proof. ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾, i.e., standing still, turning their eyes about in bewilderment and confusion, or awaiting what will befall them.

﴿And the earth shall shine with the light of its Lord﴾: that is, because He, glorified is He, will manifest Himself to them for the establishment of justice and recompense.

﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73]: i.e., with a driving of honour and dignity, to hasten them to the abode of honour. ﴿In groups﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73]: i.e., differing according to the differences in their ranks of excellence. ﴿Until, when they reach it, and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you have done well"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73]: i.e., cleansed from the filth of sins, and purified from the impurity of faults.

﴿So enter it, abiding therein﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73]: Al-Samin said: In the response to *idha* (when) there are three possibilities:

First: His saying "and its gates are opened," with the *waw* being extra. This is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The *waw* is used here rather than in the one before it, because the gates of prisons are closed until the perpetrator of the crime comes to them, whereupon they are opened for him and then closed upon him; this fits the absence of the *waw* in that case, unlike the gates of joy and happiness, which are opened in anticipation of those who will enter them.

The second: that the response is His saying "and its keepers say to them," with the *waw* again being extra.

The third: that the response is omitted. Al-Zamakhshari said: Its proper estimate is after "abiding therein"; i.e., because after the complements of the condition comes what is conjoined to it. The estimate is: "they were at rest." Al-Mubarrad estimated it as: "they were made happy." On these two views, the clause "and its gates are opened" is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), and the *waw* is the *waw* of circumstance; i.e., they came to it with its gates opened, just as "gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them" [Sad: 50] explicitly states "opened" as a circumstantial qualifier. This is the view of al-Mubarrad, al-Farisi and a group. Some claimed that this *waw* is called the *waw* of eight, because the gates of Paradise are eight. This was refuted in *al-Mughni* on the grounds that if there were a true *waw* of eight, the verse would not be one of them, since it contains no mention of a number at all, but only the word "gates," which is a plural denoting a specific number. Moreover, the *waw* does not enter upon the number itself, but upon a sentence in which it occurs. End of quotation.

That is: and it, according to its proponent, is the *waw* that enters upon the word "eight" in enumerating numbers, on the understanding that some Arabs, when counting, say "six, seven, and eight," indicating that seven is a complete number and what follows it is a new number, so it resembles the *waw* of resumption.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[74–75] ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, that we may settle in the Garden wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the doers [of good]."﴾ ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with the praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 74–75]

﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us"﴾, meaning: by bringing us to what He promised us, and what He informed us of through the tongues of His messengers. ﴿And has caused us to inherit the earth﴾, meaning: the earth of the Hereafter. He likened their attaining it through their deeds to their inheriting from their fathers, as though their deeds were their fathers, as it was said:

*"My father is Islam; I have no father other than it."*

And as it is said: "Truthfulness brings about salvation." ﴿That we may settle in the Garden wherever we will﴾, meaning: each of them settles in his spacious garden in whatever place he wishes. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the doers [of good]﴾, meaning: those who acted upon what they knew. ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75], meaning: the heavenly angels, surrounding, in the Garden of Firdaws, the Throne of the Most Merciful, encircling it. The discussion concerning the bearers of the Throne was already mentioned in the commentary on the verse ﴿Then He rose over the Throne﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54] in Surat al-A'raf, so recall it.

﴿Exalting [Allah] with the praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75], meaning: between the creatures. ﴿With truth﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75], meaning: with justice. ﴿And it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75], meaning: for what He judged between them with truth, and placed each in his rightful station. The speaker is either the Truth, glorious is His majesty, or the encircling angels, or the believers among those judged between, or all of them; so to Him belongs praise, mighty and majestic is He.

On the authority of Qatadah, he said: "Allah began the creation with *Al-hamdu lillah* (Praise be to Allah), saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [Al-An'am: 1], and He concluded with praise, saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds'﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75]."
